title: Longest Square Streak in an Array
statement:
Choose a subsequence of the integer array `nums` (delete any number of elements, possibly none, keeping the rest in their original order). Call it a *square streak* when it has two or more elements and, after you sort it in increasing order, each element other than the first is exactly the square of the element just before it.

Return the length of the longest square streak you can choose, or `-1` when no square streak exists.
notes:
## Intuition

Order and position do not matter: a subsequence can pick any values, and the streak is judged after sorting. So the question is really about which distinct values are present. A streak is a chain `x, x², x⁴, ...`, and since every value is at most 10^5, a chain can have at most 5 members (`2, 4, 16, 256, 65536`). Trying every subsequence is hopeless, but following each chain with a set lookup is cheap.

## Approach

1. Put every value into a set `seen` so membership checks take O(1).
2. For each distinct value `start`, set `current = start` and `length = 0`.
3. While `current` is in `seen`, count it and replace `current` by its square.
4. Keep the largest `length` in `best`.
5. A streak needs at least two members, so return `best` if it is 2 or more, else `-1`.

## Example 1, step by step

`seen = {4, 3, 6, 16, 8, 2}`. From `4`: `4` and `16` are present, `256` is not, so `length = 2`. From `3`, `6` and `8`: their squares are missing, so `length = 1`. From `16`: `length = 1`. From `2`: `2`, `4` and `16` are present and `256` is not, so `length = 3`. `best = 3`, which is at least 2, so the answer is `3`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): building the set is O(n), and each walk takes at most 5 steps because the squares pass 10^5 quickly.
- Space: O(n) for the set.

## Pitfalls

- A single value is not a streak: `best = 1` must turn into `-1`.
- Duplicates cannot both be used in one chain (`2, 2` is not a streak because `2² ≠ 2`); the set removes them naturally.
- Squares grow fast; in languages with 32-bit integers, `65536 * 65536` overflows, so use a 64-bit type or stop once the value passes 10^5.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `seen` | set of the distinct values in `nums` |
| `best` | longest chain found so far |
| `start` | the value a chain is followed from |
| `current` | the next value the chain needs |
| `length` | how many chain members were found from `start` |

narration.2: Store the distinct values in a set so each chain step is a constant-time lookup.
narration.3: No chain has been found yet.
narration.5: Try following a chain from every distinct value.
narration.6: Count how many chain members exist from this start.
narration.7: The first member the chain needs is the start value itself.
narration.8: Keep walking while the needed value is present.
narration.9: It is present, so the chain grows by one.
narration.10: The next member must be the square of this one.
narration.12: Remember the longest chain seen so far.
narration.14: A streak needs at least two members; otherwise report -1.
